messages.subject: patch for lstar
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
  I'm not sure if this is the right forum for bug reports/patches, so
let me know if there's a different mailing list.

  The gradient in lstar (in the file lstar.R) uses the initial values
of phi1 and phi2 (the linear parameters) for each evaluation, and
doesn't change them to reflect different values of gamma and theta
(the nonlinear parameters).  The gradient is also scaled by the number
of observations, but the objective function isn't.  The included patch
makes the changes.  After making the change, the example for
selectLSTAR in selectHyperParams.Rd fails (it tries to use a negative
value of gamma)... sorry for not fixing that, but I couldn't think of
a good way.

--Gray Calhoun

patch follows:

--- R/lstar.R	2009-12-25 07:49:46.000000000 -0600
+++ ../tsDyn-patch/lstar.R	2010-07-14 15:46:54.000000000 -0500
@@ -137,11 +137,16 @@ lstar <- function(x, m, d=1, steps=d, se
   # Computes the gradient
   #
   # Returns the gradient with respect to the error
-  gradEhat <- function(p, phi1, phi2)
+  gradEhat <- function(p)
     {
       gamma <- p[1]  #Extract parms from vector p
       th          <- p[2] 	     #Extract parms from vector p

+      xx <- cbind(xxL, xxH * G(z, gamma, th))
+      tmp <- lm.fit(xx, yy)$coefficients
+      phi1 <- tmp[1:(mL+1)]
+      phi2 <- tmp[(mL+2):(mL+mH+2)]
+
       y.hat <- F(phi1, phi2, gamma, th)
       e.hat <- yy - y.hat

@@ -151,7 +156,7 @@ lstar <- function(x, m, d=1, steps=d, se
       gGamma <- as.vector(xxH %*% phi2) * as.vector(dfX * (z - th));
       gTh <-        - as.vector(xxH %*% phi2) * as.vector(gamma *
dfX);

-      J = - cbind(gGamma, gTh) / sqrt(str$n.used)
+      J = - cbind(gGamma, gTh)

       return(2 * t(e.hat) %*% J)

@@ -159,7 +164,7 @@ lstar <- function(x, m, d=1, steps=d, se

   #Sum of squares function
   #p: vector of parameters
-  SS <- function(p, phi1, phi2) {
+  SS <- function(p) {
     gamma <- p[1]   #Extract parms from vector p
     th <- p[2]      #Extract parms from vector p

@@ -182,7 +187,7 @@ lstar <- function(x, m, d=1, steps=d, se
   #Numerical minimization##########
   p <- c(gamma, th)   #pack parameters in one vector
   res <- optim(p, SS, gradEhat, hessian = TRUE, method="BFGS",
-               control = control, phi1 = phi1, phi2 = phi2)
+               control = control)

   if(trace)
     if(res$convergence!=0)

messages.subject: Re: Help on STAR model
messages.body_plain:
Dear Eric,
   The software I used is included in the R package tsDyn, which you can find
at http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tsDyn/index.html However, the STAR
implementation is still a development version, so you will have
to be careful.
   The tsDyn package is a small package being developed by some volunteers. We
are always in need of help, so if you can find any way to help (correct bugs,
complete documentation etc), don't hesitate to contact the developers at the
mailing list ts...@googlegroups.com
   Best regards,

--
Jos� Luis Aznarte M.
